limitations_and_boundaries: The study focuses on primary human fibroblasts; generalizability to other cell types is partially addressed (fig. S11) but not fully explored.
The role of the endoplasmic reticulum and membranous sheets in the diffusion barrier is noted but not mechanistically dissected.
The paper does not provide direct force measurements on the nucleus; piston action is inferred from pressure and movement data.
The study does not examine the role of other nesprin isoforms or LINC complex components beyond nesprin 3.
The in vivo relevance of the lobopodial migration mode is not tested.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.

provenance.text_excerpt: Because nesprin 3, a nucleoskeleton-vimentin linker protein, is a proposed mediator of force transmission through the cytoskeleton to the nucleus needed for polarity and migration (14), we searched for an actomyosin-vimentin-nesprin 3 complex.
